the design of a PD like discrete-time consensus algorithm for the distributed discrete-time coordinated tracking problem where only a subset of vehicles can obtain the reference state and the communication between the vehicles is intermittent.
the design of distributed tracking algorithms that are robust with respect to the time varying reference state, the sampling period and the communication network.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed discrete time consensus algorithm can achieve the desired tracking performance for a team of vehicles with a time varying state reference and limited communication, which is a significant contribution to the existing work on distributed control for a team of autonomous vehicles with a time invariant state reference.
the proposed PD like consensus algorithm is able to achieve a smaller tracking error than the existing P like consensus algorithm under the same communication graph and the same sampling period.
the PD like discrete time tracking algorithm is more robust to the sampling period than the P like algorithm.

the proposed discrete time PD like consensus algorithm can provide better tracking performance than an existing discrete time P like consensus algorithm.
a PD like discrete control law is a viable alternative for distributed discrete time tracking of a time varying reference.
